chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, raising it to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him),
he said: 'The one who applies perfume at the inception of the day, his intellect would not cease to be with him up to the night.'
And he said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'A prayer performed whilst perfumed is superior to seventy prayers without perfuming.'

key_terms.أَوَّلَ النَّهَارِ: at the inception of the day

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of wearing perfume during prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links physical purity with intellectual clarity, suggesting that the pleasant scent of perfume aids in maintaining focus and 'aql (intellect) throughout the day. The comparison to seventy prayers underscores the significance of external adornment as a reflection of internal reverence, elevating the quality of worship through sensory engagement.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, 
(It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
having said: ‘The one who applies perfume at the inception of the day his intellect would not cease to be with him up to the night’.
And he (the narrator) said: ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘A Salaat (Prayer) performed whilst perfumed is superior than seventy Salaat without perfuming’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated in a marfu‘ manner has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
has said, ‘If one uses perfume in the beginning of the day, his power of reason continues to work until the night.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘Performing one Salat (prayer) with perfume is better than seventy Salat (prayer) without perfume.’”
